text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 13 in history.
54 - Roman emperor Claudius I died after eating poisoned mushrooms given to him by his wife, the Empress Agrippina.
1792 - The cornerstone of the U.S. president's official residence, The White House in Washington, DC., was laid by George Washington.
1812 - British forces defeated the Americans at the Battle of Queenston Heights, Ontario, helping to put an end to the U.S. attempt to invade Canada.
1815 - Joachim Murat, cavalry leader who was one of Napoleon's most famous marshals and king of Naples, 1808-15, died.
1884 - Greenwich was established as the universal time meridian of longitude from which standard times throughout the world are calculated (Greenwich Mean Time).
1923 - The Turkish Grand National Assembly declared Ankara the capital of Turkey.

1925 - Margaret Thatcher, British Conservative politician, born Margaret Hilda Roberts. She became Britain's first woman prime minister in 1979 and was the longest-serving British premier this century until she was unceremoniously ousted by a revolt within her own party in November, 1990.
1943 - Italy declared war on its former Axis partner Germany.
1962 - Drama critics applauded the opening in New York of Edward Albee's first full-length play, "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf".
1964 - Three Soviet cosmonauts manning the world's first multi-seat spacecraft, Voshkod, landed safely after a 24-hour journey.
1970 - Fiji became the 127th member of the United Nations.
1972 - A Soviet Ilyushin-62 crashed near Moscow airport, killing all 176 on board in what, at the time, was the worst disaster in civilian aviation history.

1976 - A Boeing 707 cargo plane on charter to a Bolivian company, lost an engine after takeoff from Santa Cruz and ploughed into the city's main street. The 3 crew were killed along with over 100 on the ground.
1977 - Four Palestinian terrorists hijacked a Lufthansa airliner over the Mediterranean in support of their allies in the Baader-Meinhof group.
1988 - The Shroud of Turin, revered by many Christians as Christ's burial cloth, was shown by carbon-dating tests to be a fake from the Middle Ages.
1990 - Lebanon's General Michel Aoun surrendered to Syrian-backed President Elias Hrawi -- his two years of defiance ended in minutes by a Syrian air raid.
1990 - The plaintive echoes of Slavonic chant drifted across Red Square as the first Russian Orthodox service for more than 70 years was held in St Basil's Cathedral, next to the Kremlin.
1993 - Guenter Parche, the man who admitted stabbing tennis star Monica Seles, was given a two-year suspended sentence in Hamburg for causing her grievous bodily harm.
1994 - Northern Ireland's Loyalist terror groups announced a ceasefire to match that from the Irish Republican Army.

1995 - Austrian deputies dissolved parliament as a prelude to a snap general election following the collapse of the coalition government. It was the shortest-lived parliament in the history of Austria's postwar Second Republic.
1995 - France rejected appeals to abandon nuclear tests in the South Pacific after ban-the-bomb scientist Joseph Rotblat won the 1995 Nobel Peace Prize.
1995 - Failure by 42 governments to agree international curbs on the use of land mines provoked outrage among humanitarian groups and anti-mine campaigners.
